transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because I just feel worn down almost all the time. It doesn't really seem to matter if I get a full night’s sleep, I still feel it. By the time I’ve handled work and tried to deal with the house clutter, I just... I have very little energy left for anything else.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yeah, I'd say so. It's been going on for a while, actually. Most days there’s just this... low, gray mood running in the background. I mean, I can still go into the lab and talk to people, so I'm getting my work done. But I just don’t really feel light or excited about things the way I used to. Even with stuff I usually enjoy, like baking or checking the telescope on a clear night, the feeling just isn't there anymore.
Have you noticed that you take less pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in them altogether?

Yeah, like I was just saying with the baking and the telescope... I'd definitely say I take less pleasure in them. I wouldn't say I've lost interest completely, because I still try to do them sometimes, but... yeah, the enjoyment just isn't really there right now.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy levels or an increase in fatigue during this time?

Yeah, like I mentioned when we first started talking, that's actually the main reason I decided to come in. I just feel worn down almost all the time. It doesn't really seem to matter if I get a full night's sleep, the fatigue is still there. By the time I get through my work at the lab and try to deal with the clutter around the house, my energy is just spent. I have very little left in the tank for anything else.
Have you been having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early in the morning?

No, my sleep is actually pretty normal. I fall asleep fine, and I usually sleep straight through the night. I don't wake up super early or anything like that. Like I said, I get a full night's sleep, I just still feel tired anyway. But the sleep itself hasn't been an issue.
Have you been feeling like you’re not worth much or that you’re letting people down, or have you been blaming yourself for things more than usual?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel worthless or anything. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes for not having the energy to keep the house clean or do my hobbies, but I don't think I'm letting people down or blaming myself for things out of the ordinary. It's just the tiredness that's getting to me.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or have other people commented that you're moving or speaking more slowly? Or on the flip side, have you felt restless or fidgety lately?

No, neither of those. I don't think I'm moving or talking any slower than normal, and nobody's pointed anything like that out to me. And I haven't felt restless or fidgety, either. Just... tired, like I said.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently?
No, not really. My appetite has been pretty normal. I'm eating about the same as I usually do, and my weight hasn't changed either, at least not that I've noticed.
Have you had episodes of feeling this way before, or is this the first time you've experienced these symptoms?

I wouldn't really call them episodes, because it doesn't really come and go. It's more just... this low baseline that's been pretty constant. It started shortly after we moved into our older house, so... a little over two years ago now.
Have you ever had a period of time before this one where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks?

No, I don't think so. Before this started a couple of years ago, I felt fine. I mean, I'd have a bad day here or there like anyone else, but never a stretch of two weeks or more where I felt down or lost interest in things. This is really the first time I've dealt with anything like this.
Have there ever been times when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely confident — maybe even so much that it affected your judgment or behavior?

No, never anything like that. I've never had a time where I felt... unusually high or had that kind of extreme energy. I'm a pretty level-headed person, so I definitely haven't experienced anything that affected my judgment or made me overly confident. It's really just been that constant low mood I mentioned.
Have you had any periods of at least two months where you felt better — where your mood improved and your energy levels returned to normal — at any point since this started two years ago?

No, I haven't. I mean, I might have a day or two here and there where things feel a little lighter, but... no, definitely never a stretch of two months where my energy came back or I felt normal again. It's just been that same low baseline the whole time.
Was there anything specific going on in your life around the time this started — like stress at work, family issues, or anything traumatic — or did it seem to come on without any clear trigger?

No, not really. I've actually thought about that, but... there wasn't any major event or trauma or anything like that. Work was just the usual amount of busy, and things at home were fine. It really just seemed to come on without any clear trigger. It just sort of crept up on me over time.
Have these symptoms caused you noticeable problems in your daily life — like at work, in your relationships, or in your ability to take care of things at home?

Yeah, it's definitely affecting things, though maybe not in a dramatic way. At work—I'm a physical scientist—I'm still getting my regular lab work done, but... things like drafting grants or making routine decisions about projects, it all just takes me noticeably longer than it used to. I just can't seem to focus or push through it like before. And at home, I've really let my hobbies go. I used to bake a lot, take care of my bonsai trees, and I had all these plans for my telescope, which gave my downtime some structure. But lately, I've just stopped keeping up with all of it.
Have you ever felt so worn down or low that it was hard to carry out your basic daily responsibilities, like getting dressed, cooking meals, or showing up to work?

No, it hasn't been quite that bad. I mean, I still get up, get dressed, and go to the lab every day. I haven't missed work or anything like that. And I can still manage the basics at home, like throwing a simple dinner together or doing the laundry... it just feels like more of a chore than it used to. But no, I haven't been completely unable to do those basic daily things. It hasn't stopped me from functioning on that level.

Have these symptoms interfered with your ability to function in any other ways, like maintaining relationships, participating in social activities, or meeting your usual standards for performance at work?

Not really, no. I think I pretty much covered it. My relationships are fine... I still see my friends and family, even if I'm maybe a bit less talkative lately. Socially, I still show up to things, I just don't really go out of my way to organize them anymore. 

And at work, the actual quality of what I do is still up to my usual standards. I'm not making mistakes in the lab or handing in bad data. It just... like I said, it just takes me a lot longer to get through the planning and the paperwork. So, no, nothing else really stands out.
Have you ever noticed that your thoughts are slowed down or that you can't think clearly, or that it's hard to make decisions even about small things?

Yeah, actually, that's exactly it. My mind just feels... slower. Like, tasks that used to be pretty clean and sequential for me, um, like revising a paragraph for a grant or even just figuring out what materials I need for a small repair around the house... they just take me noticeably longer now. I just find myself second-guessing really small decisions. It's frustrating because I know I can do it, but the thinking part just feels like wading through mud.
